# Resource: stripe_identity_verification_session

A Stripe Identity check of one person's document or ID number. Set `status` to `canceled` to cancel a session that still requires input. The `client_secret` and `url` that start the check are sensitive and stay in the state. Redacting a session is not a resource: redact it with Stripe's API, after which Stripe no longer serves it. Verification flows and related persons are not available, so `type` is required. `type` and `metadata` change in place; changing `options` or `provided_details`, or any argument that only a create takes, fails the plan.

~> Stripe cannot delete a verification session; set `status` to `canceled` to cancel one that still requires input. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the identity verification session, fail at plan time. To stop managing an identity verification session, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_customer" "applicant" {
  email = "applicant@example.com"
}

# Send the person to the session's `url`, or hand the `client_secret` to Stripe.js.
resource "stripe_identity_verification_session" "kyc" {
  type             = "document"
  related_customer = stripe_customer.applicant.id

  options = {
    document = {
      allowed_types        = ["passport", "driving_license"]
      require_live_capture = true
    }
  }
}

output "verification_url" {
  value     = stripe_identity_verification_session.kyc.url
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `type` - (Required) The type of [verification check](https://docs.stripe.com/identity/verification-checks) to be performed. You must provide a `type` if not passing `verification_flow`. Possible values: `document`, `id_number`.

The following arguments are optional:

* `client_reference_id` - (Optional) A string to reference this user. This can be a customer ID, a session ID, or similar, and can be used to reconcile this verification with your internal systems. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `options` - (Optional) A set of options for the session’s verification checks. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`options`](#options) below.
* `provided_details` - (Optional) Details provided about the user being verified. These details might be shown to the user. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. See [`provided_details`](#provided_details) below.
* `related_customer` - (Optional) Customer ID Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `related_customer_account` - (Optional) The ID of the Account representing a customer. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `return_url` - (Optional) The URL that the user will be redirected to upon completing the verification flow. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `status` - (Optional) Status of this VerificationSession. [Learn more about the lifecycle of sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/identity/how-sessions-work). Possible values: `canceled`. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.

<a id="options"></a>
### `options`

The `options` attribute supports:

* `document` - (Optional) See [`options.document`](#options.document) below.
* `email` - (Read-Only) See [`options.email`](#options.email) below.
* `matching` - (Read-Only) See [`options.matching`](#options.matching) below.
* `phone` - (Read-Only) See [`options.phone`](#options.phone) below.

<a id="options.document"></a>
### `options.document`

The `options.document` attribute supports:

* `allowed_types` - (Optional) Array of strings of allowed identity document types. If the provided identity document isn’t one of the allowed types, the verification check will fail with a document_type_not_allowed error code. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `require_id_number` - (Optional) Collect an ID number and perform an [ID number check](https://docs.stripe.com/identity/verification-checks?type=id-number) with the document’s extracted name and date of birth. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `require_live_capture` - (Optional) Disable image uploads, identity document images have to be captured using the device’s camera. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `require_matching_selfie` - (Optional) Capture a face image and perform a [selfie check](https://docs.stripe.com/identity/verification-checks?type=selfie) comparing a photo ID and a picture of your user’s face. [Learn more](https://docs.stripe.com/identity/selfie). Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="options.email"></a>
### `options.email`

The `options.email` attribute supports:

* `require_verification` - Request one time password verification of `provided_details.email`.

<a id="options.matching"></a>
### `options.matching`

The `options.matching` attribute supports:

* `dob` - Strictness of the DOB matching policy to apply. Possible values: `none`, `similar`.
* `name` - Strictness of the name matching policy to apply. Possible values: `none`, `similar`.

<a id="options.phone"></a>
### `options.phone`

The `options.phone` attribute supports:

* `require_verification` - Request one time password verification of `provided_details.phone`.

<a id="provided_details"></a>
### `provided_details`

The `provided_details` attribute supports:

* `email` - (Optional) Email of user being verified
* `phone` - (Optional) Phone number of user being verified

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `client_secret` - (Sensitive) The short-lived client secret used by Stripe.js to [show a verification modal](https://docs.stripe.com/js/identity/modal) inside your app. This client secret expires after 24 hours and can only be used once. Don’t store it, log it, embed it in a URL, or expose it to anyone other than the user. Make sure that you have TLS enabled on any page that includes the client secret. Refer to our docs on [passing the client secret to the frontend](https://docs.stripe.com/identity/verification-sessions#client-secret) to learn more.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `last_error` - If present, this property tells you the last error encountered when processing the verification. See [`last_error`](#last_error) below.
* `last_verification_report` - ID of the most recent VerificationReport. [Learn more about accessing detailed verification results.](https://docs.stripe.com/identity/verification-sessions#results)
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `redaction` - Redaction status of this VerificationSession. If the VerificationSession is not redacted, this field will be null. See [`redaction`](#redaction) below.
* `url` - (Sensitive) The short-lived URL that you use to redirect a user to Stripe to submit their identity information. This URL expires after 48 hours and can only be used once. Don’t store it, log it, send it in emails or expose it to anyone other than the user. Refer to our docs on [verifying identity documents](https://docs.stripe.com/identity/verify-identity-documents?platform=web&type=redirect) to learn how to redirect users to Stripe.
* `verified_outputs` - (Sensitive) The user’s verified data. See [`verified_outputs`](#verified_outputs) below.

<a id="last_error"></a>
### `last_error`

The `last_error` attribute supports:

* `code` - A short machine-readable string giving the reason for the verification or user-session failure. Possible values: `abandoned`, `consent_declined`, `country_not_supported`, `device_not_supported`, `document_expired`, `document_type_not_supported`, `document_unverified_other`, `email_unverified_other`, `email_verification_declined`, `id_number_insufficient_document_data`, `id_number_mismatch`, `id_number_unverified_other`, `phone_unverified_other`, `phone_verification_declined`, `selfie_document_missing_photo`, `selfie_face_mismatch`, `selfie_manipulated`, `selfie_unverified_other`, `under_supported_age`.
* `reason` - A message that explains the reason for verification or user-session failure.

<a id="redaction"></a>
### `redaction`

The `redaction` attribute supports:

* `status` - Indicates whether this object and its related objects have been redacted or not. Possible values: `processing`, `redacted`, `validated`.

<a id="verified_outputs"></a>
### `verified_outputs`

The `verified_outputs` attribute supports:

* `address` - The user's verified address. See [`verified_outputs.address`](#verified_outputs.address) below.
* `dob` - The user’s verified date of birth. See [`verified_outputs.dob`](#verified_outputs.dob) below.
* `email` - The user's verified email address
* `first_name` - The user's verified first name.
* `id_number` - The user's verified id number.
* `id_number_type` - The user's verified id number type. Possible values: `br_cpf`, `sg_nric`, `us_ssn`.
* `last_name` - The user's verified last name.
* `phone` - The user's verified phone number
* `sex` - The user's verified sex. Possible values: `[redacted]`, `female`, `male`, `unknown`.
* `unparsed_place_of_birth` - The user's verified place of birth as it appears in the document.
* `unparsed_sex` - The user's verified sex as it appears in the document.

<a id="verified_outputs.address"></a>
### `verified_outputs.address`

The `verified_outputs.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="verified_outputs.dob"></a>
### `verified_outputs.dob`

The `verified_outputs.dob` attribute supports:

* `day` - Numerical day between 1 and 31.
* `month` - Numerical month between 1 and 12.
* `year` - The four-digit year.

## Removing from State

To stop managing an identity verification session whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_identity_verification_session.kyc

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_identity_verification_session.kyc
```

The identity verification session stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import an identity verification session using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_identity_verification_session.kyc
  id = "vs_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_identity_verification_session.kyc
  identity = {
    id = "vs_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the identity verification session.

Using `terraform import`, import an identity verification session using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_identity_verification_session.kyc vs_123
```

~> Stripe does not return `provided_details`, so an imported session has none in state and the next plan replaces it if the configuration sets some. Stripe does not return `return_url`, so an imported identity verification session has it null: a configuration that sets it plans a replacement after the import.
